reason: E1 supports dynamic softening and friction reduction via grain refinement but does not demonstrate a switch to grain boundary sliding or formation of an amorphous–crystalline layer. E2 shows grain refinement and amorphous–crystalline layers in worn TiNbZr alloys, but these are not HEA coatings and the amorphous layer is linked to Ag addition, not solely grain size below 20 nm. The key premises about the deformation mechanism switch and adaptive layer formation are thus only partially supported by the cited evidence.
premises: Grain refinement below ~20 nm suppresses dislocation plasticity and promotes grain boundary sliding
Grain boundary sliding leads to dynamic softening (inverse Hall–Petch) and lower shear strength
This softening reduces friction and enhances wear resistance
An adaptive amorphous–crystalline surface layer forms during wear of refined HEA coatings
